label: Umbrella review protocol
framework: JBI umbrella review guidance with PRIOR-informed overview reporting

items.requirement: Identify the document as an umbrella review protocol.
items.prompt: What is the umbrella review title and topic area?
items.helpText: Umbrella reviews synthesize existing systematic reviews or meta-analyses.
items.exampleResponse: Umbrella review protocol: effects of school-based nutrition interventions on child health outcomes.

items.requirement: Explain why an overview of reviews is needed.
items.prompt: Why is a review of existing systematic reviews more appropriate than a new primary-study review?
items.helpText: Mention evidence volume, overlapping reviews, discordant conclusions, or decision needs.
items.exampleResponse: Multiple systematic reviews report overlapping but discordant findings, creating uncertainty for guideline developers.

items.requirement: State the review question for systematic reviews.
items.prompt: What population, intervention/exposure, comparator, outcome, and review type will define eligibility?
items.helpText: The unit of inclusion is usually a systematic review, not each primary study.
items.exampleResponse: We will include systematic reviews of school nutrition interventions compared with usual practice for child health outcomes.

items.requirement: State the review objectives clearly and in alignment with the review type.
items.prompt: What are the primary and secondary objectives this protocol will guide?
items.helpText: Objectives should match the review type: estimate, map, explain, synthesize experiences, compare reviews, or maintain living evidence. State objectives for summarising and comparing existing systematic reviews.
items.exampleResponse: The primary objective is to synthesize the available evidence for the defined question. Secondary objectives include identifying gaps and describing implications for decision-makers.

items.requirement: Specify eligible review products and overlap handling.
items.prompt: Which types of reviews are eligible, and how will overlapping primary studies be managed?
items.helpText: State whether rapid reviews, scoping reviews, narrative reviews, and primary studies are excluded.
items.exampleResponse: We will include systematic reviews with explicit searches and eligibility criteria; overlap will be assessed using citation matrices.

items.prompt: Which databases, repositories, registers, websites, expert sources, and grey literature sources will be searched?
items.helpText: Information sources should fit the review type and include enough coverage to reduce avoidable bias. Prioritize review repositories and databases indexing systematic reviews.
items.exampleResponse: We will search bibliographic databases, specialist registers, organizational repositories, relevant websites, and reference lists of included sources.

items.prompt: Which databases and review repositories will be searched for existing reviews?
items.helpText: Include sources such as Epistemonikos, Cochrane Library, MEDLINE, and discipline-specific databases.
items.exampleResponse: We will search Epistemonikos, Cochrane Library, MEDLINE, Embase, Campbell Library, and reference lists of included reviews.

items.prompt: How will records or sources be screened and selected, and how will disagreements or uncertainty be handled?
items.helpText: Specify screening stages, reviewer numbers, piloting or calibration, software, reasons for exclusion, and documentation. Describe screening of review products and handling of overlapping primary studies.
items.exampleResponse: Screening criteria will be piloted. Records will be screened at title/abstract and full-text stages, with disagreements resolved by discussion or a third reviewer.

items.requirement: Describe extraction, coding, charting, or data transformation.
items.prompt: What data elements will be extracted or charted, and how will accuracy and consistency be checked?
items.helpText: Match the extraction fields to the review type and planned synthesis. Extract review-level characteristics, included study counts, conclusions, and overlap data.
items.exampleResponse: A piloted form will capture bibliographic details, study characteristics, population/context, methods, findings, limitations, and fields needed for synthesis.

items.requirement: Describe appraisal of included systematic reviews.
items.prompt: Which tool will assess review quality or methodological confidence?
items.helpText: AMSTAR 2 or JBI critical appraisal for systematic reviews are common choices.
items.exampleResponse: Two reviewers will use AMSTAR 2 to appraise included systematic reviews.

items.prompt: How will review findings, overlap, quality, and certainty be summarized?
items.helpText: Umbrella reviews usually avoid double-counting primary studies and may summarize evidence by outcome domain.
items.exampleResponse: We will summarize effect directions, overlap, AMSTAR 2 ratings, and certainty by outcome using structured tables.

items.requirement: Plan assessment of certainty, confidence, or credibility where relevant.
items.prompt: How will certainty, confidence, or credibility in the body of evidence or findings be assessed?
items.helpText: Use GRADE, GRADE-CERQual, review confidence ratings, or a justified alternative where applicable. Describe how review quality, overlap, and certainty will influence conclusions.
items.exampleResponse: Confidence will be assessed using a framework appropriate to the evidence type and reported alongside the main findings.

items.requirement: Describe planned outputs and dissemination routes.
items.prompt: What outputs will be produced, who are the audiences, and how will findings be shared?
items.helpText: Consider manuscripts, briefs, map products, stakeholder reports, datasets, presentations, guideline inputs, and update notices. Consider manuscripts, briefs, map products, stakeholder reports, datasets, presentations, guideline inputs, and update notices.
items.exampleResponse: Findings will be shared through a manuscript, technical report, decision brief, presentation, and accessible summary for stakeholders.

items.requirement: Identify appendices required for transparency and reproducibility.
items.prompt: Which appendices will be included to document methods and decisions?
items.helpText: Appendices may include search strategies, screening forms, extraction forms, appraisal tools, coding frameworks, stakeholder materials, and amendment logs. Include overlap matrix, AMSTAR-style appraisal form, and extraction template.
items.exampleResponse: Appendices will include database search strategies, screening forms, extraction templates, appraisal tools, coding framework, and protocol amendments.
